question: Estimate Punctual Pros revenue from public filings
html:
Punctual Pros Revenue Estimate

Public filings put Punctual Pros' FY2025 pro forma revenue at about $22M est. (range $16-28M): roughly $18M from Pennsylvania and $3-5M from the New Jersey add-on (Punctual Pros public filings). Confidence is medium, and the figure combines three indirect methods.

How the estimate is built

  • PPP baseline. The Rohrer Company's April 2020 PPP loan of $745,985 implies ~$3.58M of 2019 payroll. That suggests ~50-58 employees and ~$9-12M of 2019 revenue (est.) (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • Headcount scaling. About 113 employees by 2024, at ~$76K Lancaster wages and a 40-45% labor ratio, supports an $18-22M Pennsylvania run-rate (est.). The 113 figure has not been re-verified (BSP firm profile).
  • Franchise disclosure cross-check. The 2026 FDD lists 25 territories: 19 in Pennsylvania and 6 in New Jersey. Mapping them to Item 19 quartiles gives ~$12-19M for Pennsylvania and ~$3-5M for New Jersey (est.) (Punctual Pros public filings).

Key figures

MetricEstimateConfidence
FY2025 PA revenue~$18M (range $12-24M) est.Medium
FY2025 pro forma total~$22M (range $16-28M) est.Medium
Revenue per territory~$0.9M est.Low
Franchise fees to Authority Brands~$1.6M a year (~7.2-7.5% of revenue) est.—
Adjusted EBITDA~$1.8-3.1M, central ~$2.6M est.Low

Where the estimate is weak

  • Per-territory revenue. About $0.9M per territory sits well above system averages of $0.61-0.66M for One Hour and Ben Franklin. This could mean real outperformance or an overstated blend. The filings do not settle which.
  • Margin ceiling. Royalty plus brand fund caps adjusted EBITDA margins at about 8-14% (est.). Small revenue errors therefore move EBITDA a lot.
  • Horvath standalone. The 2019 PPP data imply only ~$3-4M of revenue (est.). Growth since then is not observable in the filings.

Debt context

  • PGIM Private Credit Fund's June 30, 2026 10-Q shows a first-lien loan to Punctual Pros Midco, LLC (Punctual Pros public filings):
  • $4.83M funded at 8.73%, maturing March 26, 2029.
  • Marked at ~98.6% of par.
  • A further $1.4M unfunded.
  • This is one lender's disclosed position. Total debt is not visible in the filings.

What would firm this up

  • Monthly revenue by brand and territory for FY2025 from the portfolio company's general ledger.
  • Royalty statements paid to Authority Brands. Revenue can be backed out directly from the 6% royalty.
  • Current payroll registers to replace the headcount estimate.

Next actions

  1. Pull FY2025 royalty reports and reconcile them to the ~$22M est. figure.
  2. Compare revenue per territory against Item 19 quartiles, brand by brand, to test the outperformance claim.
  3. Confirm current headcount and labor ratio with Punctual Pros finance.
  4. Obtain the full credit agreement to size total leverage against the ~$2.6M est. EBITDA.

# Punctual Pros Revenue Estimate

Public filings put Punctual Pros' FY2025 pro forma revenue at about **$22M est. (range $16-28M)**: roughly $18M from Pennsylvania and $3-5M from the New Jersey add-on (Punctual Pros public filings). Confidence is medium, and the figure combines three indirect methods.

## How the estimate is built

- **PPP baseline.** The Rohrer Company's April 2020 PPP loan of $745,985 implies ~$3.58M of 2019 payroll. That suggests ~50-58 employees and ~$9-12M of 2019 revenue (est.) (Punctual Pros public filings).
- **Headcount scaling.** About 113 employees by 2024, at ~$76K Lancaster wages and a 40-45% labor ratio, supports an $18-22M Pennsylvania run-rate (est.). The 113 figure has not been re-verified (BSP firm profile).
- **Franchise disclosure cross-check.** The 2026 FDD lists 25 territories: 19 in Pennsylvania and 6 in New Jersey. Mapping them to Item 19 quartiles gives ~$12-19M for Pennsylvania and ~$3-5M for New Jersey (est.) (Punctual Pros public filings).

## Key figures

| Metric | Estimate | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| FY2025 PA revenue | ~$18M (range $12-24M) est. | Medium |
| FY2025 pro forma total | ~$22M (range $16-28M) est. | Medium |
| Revenue per territory | ~$0.9M est. | Low |
| Franchise fees to Authority Brands | ~$1.6M a year (~7.2-7.5% of revenue) est. | — |
| Adjusted EBITDA | ~$1.8-3.1M, central ~$2.6M est. | Low |

## Where the estimate is weak

- **Per-territory revenue.** About $0.9M per territory sits well above system averages of $0.61-0.66M for One Hour and Ben Franklin. This could mean real outperformance or an overstated blend. The filings do not settle which.
- **Margin ceiling.** Royalty plus brand fund caps adjusted EBITDA margins at about 8-14% (est.). Small revenue errors therefore move EBITDA a lot.
- **Horvath standalone.** The 2019 PPP data imply only ~$3-4M of revenue (est.). Growth since then is not observable in the filings.

## Debt context

- PGIM Private Credit Fund's June 30, 2026 10-Q shows a first-lien loan to Punctual Pros Midco, LLC (Punctual Pros public filings):
  - $4.83M funded at 8.73%, maturing March 26, 2029.
  - Marked at ~98.6% of par.
  - A further $1.4M unfunded.
- This is one lender's disclosed position. Total debt is not visible in the filings.

## What would firm this up

- Monthly revenue by brand and territory for FY2025 from the portfolio company's general ledger.
- Royalty statements paid to Authority Brands. Revenue can be backed out directly from the 6% royalty.
- Current payroll registers to replace the headcount estimate.

## Next actions

1. Pull FY2025 royalty reports and reconcile them to the ~$22M est. figure.
2. Compare revenue per territory against Item 19 quartiles, brand by brand, to test the outperformance claim.
3. Confirm current headcount and labor ratio with Punctual Pros finance.
4. Obtain the full credit agreement to size total leverage against the ~$2.6M est. EBITDA.
